title: Modeling the SL-LET Paradigm in AUTOSAR Adaptive
problem: AUTOSAR Adaptive standard does not address non-functional requirements like determinism, which is critical for automotive functional safety guarantees in service-oriented C++ middleware running on POSIX systems.
motivation: Modern automotive systems require deterministic execution to ensure functional safety compliance, a gap in AUTOSAR Adaptive unlike earlier AUTOSAR Classic specifications.
method: The authors extend AUTOSAR Adaptive (an automotive software standard) with System-Level Logical Execution Time (SL-LET), a timing mechanism that ensures tasks execute predictably and deterministically—a requirement for automotive safety systems. They build a prototype of this extension and validate it on realistic automotive applications using the official AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Demonstrator.
key_novelty: This is the first extension of SL-LET (a model ensuring deterministic, predictable task execution) from AUTOSAR Classic to AUTOSAR Adaptive's more flexible, service-based architecture.
contributions: Modeling extension integrating SL-LET semantics into AUTOSAR Adaptive specification
Prototype implementation of SL-LET enforcement in AUTOSAR Adaptive middleware
Experimental validation on realistic automotive application via APD
limitations: Evaluation limited to single automotive application; scalability to large federated automotive networks not discussed.
